No journal-specific AI policy page found for ABT itself; only the publisher-level policy from University of California Press (which owns/hosts ABT via online.ucpress.edu) was located. UC Press policy: AI cannot be listed/credited as an author; authors may use AI to improve readability/formatting/grammar of human-written text but must disclose such use to editors and be transparent in the manuscript; AI use to generate original text/images/data analysis requires disclosure; peer reviewers are strictly prohibited from using AI tools to compose review reports or from uploading manuscripts into AI tools (copyright violation); freelance contractors/editors may not use AI to generate original content for UC Press publications. This is publisher-wide, not confirmed as reproduced verbatim in ABT's own author guidelines (the ABT-specific author-guidelines PDF linked from bioone.org could not be opened/parsed in this session).

This is Taylor & Francis's GROUP-WIDE policy, not a CoDesign-specific one (no journal-level AI policy page found). Fact: Generative AI tools cannot be listed as an author (cannot take accountability/hold copyright). Authors must disclose any GenAI use in the article via a statement naming the tool, version, and how/why it was used. Publisher frames permitted uses as copyediting/language refinement and non-native-English support, i.e. disclosure-gated use is allowed, not an outright ban. Primary policy page returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; fact is corroborated across secondary summaries (Enago TANDF AI Guidelines page, university LibGuides) that quote the same requirement, so treated as reliable despite indirect access.

此為 Oxford University Press 全出版社通用政策，非 The Monist 期刊專屬頁面（Monist 的 General Instructions 頁未提及 AI）。政策要點（依 WebSearch 摘要，非逐字引用）：生成式 AI 不得列為作者、不得承擔「主要著者責任」（產生論證、科學洞見、分析或結論）；若要在投稿中使用 AI 生成內容（含資料蒐集分析、圖表產製），須事先取得 OUP 書面許可（許可閘門=conditional）；允許不需許可的用途包括：圖片替代文字、文法拼字校對、翻譯核對、查核引用、產生摘要與關鍵詞、產生索引詞。作者對含 AI 生成內容的作品之準確性、完整性與原創性負全責。另一般說明頁提及 AI 使用需在投稿信與 Methods/Acknowledgements 中揭露。因為是出版社層級政策而非期刊客製化頁面，且未能直接 WebFetch 到原始頁面全文（頁面對自動抓取回傳導覽選單而非正文），故 signal_quality 定為 2。

Conditional — permitted for language/clarity editing (author-verified) and synthetic/simulated data for methodological development (e.g. algorithm testing); prohibited for generating primary research data (incl. synthetic neuroimaging fMRI/EEG/MEG/fNIRS or fabricated statistical output) or unsupervised generation of substantive research content; agentic AI used for research tasks (e.g. code, data pipelines) must be disclosed in Methods with tool/model name

JoCN-specific AI policy (supplements MIT Press default): AI cannot be listed as author; author fully responsible for AI-assisted content; permitted uses limited to text polishing and synthetic data for method development; hard prohibition on AI-generated primary data/images and unsupervised substantive content generation; reviewers discouraged from using AI to evaluate manuscript science but may use it to polish review text, with mandatory disclosure visible only to the handling editor.

Double-blind peer review; research articles normally reviewed by 2 external referees, a 3rd may be added if the first two reports don't allow a decision. Editors first screen for scope/fit, methodological soundness, and plagiarism before sending to review. Peer review phase 'normally' takes about 4–6 weeks per journal's own policy statement (may extend depending on submission volume) — this is a publisher-stated figure, not a first-hand reviewer-reported figure.
No outright pre-approval gate — conditional/disclosure-based: text-generation AI use is permitted subject to mandatory author disclosure; AI-generated/altered images are prohibited outright
